summary: Iteration 3 full-stack testing of new modules (AI, Documents, Admin, HR, Finance, Calendar, Analytics, Design Studio). Backend: 21/21 pytest pass after 1 fix. Frontend E2E: all module create-flows verified working end-to-end via network response capture. Found & fixed 1 backend model bug preventing Calendar event creation.
critical_code_review_comments: Same anti-pattern as iter1 recurred in models.Event: 'organizer_id: str' required but endpoint /api/events auto-assigns it from current_user, causing 422 on the frontend Calendar create-event form (which does not send organizer_id). Fixed by making organizer_id Optional[str] = None. Long-term: introduce dedicated *CreateRequest schemas so DB required fields don't leak to API surface.
AI /ai/chat streaming endpoint uses upsert without setting conversation_id in the $set doc; the non-streaming /ai/message correctly sets it. Consider aligning.

Admin modal likely doesn't use role='dialog' or [data-testid='admin-edit-modal'] on the wrapper — save-user-button is discoverable but modal container has no ARIA role; add role='dialog' + aria-modal for accessibility & easier testing.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (added TestDocuments, TestHR, TestFinance, TestCalendar, TestAdmin, TestAI classes)

success_rate.frontend: 100% for all iteration-3 module create flows verified via network responses (AI chat, Documents, HR employee, HR department, Finance transaction, Finance invoice, Calendar event, Admin edit-user modal, Design Studio save, Analytics charts, Logout)

seed_data_creation: Playwright and pytest created TEST_* prefixed departments, employees, documents, invoices, transactions, events, users. No cleanup performed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 3 modules all functional after 1 model fix (Event.organizer_id). AI Assistant confirmed working with EMERGENT_LLM_KEY (GPT-5.2 responded with 'Hello! How can I help you today?'). Admin edit-user modal opens (save-user-button visible) but its wrapper lacks role='dialog'; not a bug, just testability improvement. Calendar event creation returns 200; if item doesn't visually appear on current-month grid, that's because the test used a future month — sidebar 'upcoming events' still shows it.
rca of the issue: Calendar create-event failed with 422 in initial test run because models.Event.organizer_id was 'str' (required) while the /api/events endpoint auto-assigns it from user AFTER Pydantic validation. Frontend Calendar.js doesn't send organizer_id. Same pattern as iter1 owner_id/organization_id bug. Fix: made organizer_id Optional[str] = None. Verified with pytest + Playwright network capture (POST /api/events → 200 with organizer_id populated from auth).
